title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S → T is a morphism of schemes and E is an O_S-module (or abelian sheaf) with a stratification relative to T, i.e. an infinite-order Grothendieck connection δ = δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E). S_strat is the stratifying site (an infinitesimal-type site). Its objects are pairs (U,U') with U ⊂ S open and U ⊂ U' an infinitesimal thickening over T, as in the margin sketch U ⊂ U' over S over T. E_strat is the sheaf on this site defined by E. The previous page gave the comparison map H*_strat(S,E) → H*_DR(S,E) and announced an interpretation of H*_strat; this page starts on H^1 through torsors.

Step 1. A torsor under E_strat on S_strat consists of a torsor under (E_strat)_{(U,U')} = E_{U'} on each object (U,U'), contravariant in (U,U'). This is equivalent to an ordinary E-torsor P on S together with a stratification on P compatible with that of E. This is the torsor (crystal-of-torsors) analogue of 'crystal = module with stratification'.

Step 2. Give P^∞_{S/T}(E) its canonical stratification, the one independent of the stratification of E. This is Grothendieck's linearization functor L(E). The map δ is injective, since it is split as a map of sheaves by the augmentation P^∞(E) → E. There is an exact sequence (2'): 0 → E → P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE → 0. The quotient is the cokernel of δ, i.e. of the two morphisms E ⇉ P^∞(E). Grothendieck notes that δ is compatible with the stratifications.

Step 3. Hence a stratified E-torsor P is the same as two pieces of data:
- a stratified torsor under P^∞(E);
- a trivialization of the induced stratified torsor under P^∞(E)/δE.
Stratified torsors under P^∞(E) correspond to ordinary E-torsors P, via P ↦ P^∞_{S/T}(P), the infinite-jet torsor ([ ] 6.4). This is the torsor version of 'linearization has stratified cohomology equal to ordinary cohomology'.

Step 4 (completed on the next page). The trivialization amounts to a map of sheaves λ : P → P^∞(E)/δE satisfying the affine condition λ(x+ξ) = λ(x) + p(d^∞ξ). Compatibility with stratifications means λ lands in the horizontal subsheaf (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮. So a compatible stratification on P is equivalent to an E-equivariant map P → (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮ lying over d^∞ : E → (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮. This description is functorial in E and compatible with base change.

Upshot: this is the explicit H^1 (torsor-level) form of computing stratified (infinitesimal/crystalline-type) cohomology by the linearized resolution. In effect H^1_strat(S,E) is computed by the two-term complex E → (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮ of Zariski sheaves. Its higher analogue is the comparison of stratified cohomology with de Rham cohomology via the linearized de Rham complex.
errors: Next page: 'une stratification sur E rel. à T' should read 'sur P'. This is a slip of the pen.
First line: 'un torseur sous S_strat' should be 'sur S_strat'.

P^∞_{S/T}(E) is strictly a pro-object or formal completion. Grothendieck himself hesitates and crosses out 'préfaisceau'. Treating it as a sheaf with a stratification needs the usual care with infinite-order jets (projective limits). This is not a real gap.
The cited references [ ] are left blank.

ideas.what: Torsors under a stratified sheaf on the stratifying site equal ordinary torsors with a compatible stratification
ideas.modern_name: crystals of torsors / torsors on the infinitesimal site
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1968); Giraud for nonabelian H^1
ideas.where_published: Analogous module statement in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: P^∞_{S/T}(E) with its canonical stratification, and the exact sequence 0→E→P^∞(E)→P^∞(E)/δE→0 of stratified sheaves
ideas.modern_name: linearization L(E) and the linearized (Spencer-type) resolution
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968)

ideas.what: Stratified torsors under P^∞(E) ↔ ordinary E-torsors, via the infinite-jet torsor P^∞(P)
ideas.modern_name: linearization lemma at the level of H^1 / torsors

ideas.what: Description of a compatible stratification on an E-torsor P as an affine map λ: P → (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮ over d^∞
ideas.modern_name: explicit H^1_strat via the two-term linearized complex; affine (torsor) form of the de Rham comparison

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard torsor-level working-out of the linearization lemma, which is well known from Grothendieck's 1968 Crystals paper and Berthelot's work. Nothing appears that a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'Or un torseur sous S_strat sous E_strat' should read 'Or un torseur sur S_strat sous E_strat'.
'par voie de fonctions[?] contravariantes' likely reads 'de façon contravariante en (U,U')'.
'Nous regardons P^∞(E) comme muni d'une stratification sur S' is better read as 'comme un faisceau sur S, et comme tel il est muni d'une stratification canonique'.
Margin 'A.R.' is unclear; it is possibly an editorial note (e.g. 'à revoir').
'défini comme le conoyau des morphismes' reads more naturally as 'le conoyau du morphisme E → P^∞(E)'; the crossed-out word may be 'compléments/conoyau'.
